slots.jd.insurance-digital.about:
Position summary
Westbrook Insurance Group seeks a UX Designer to shape digital experiences for policyholders, agents and claims staff. The role sits within a hybrid team based in Des Moines, IA, and partners closely with product and engineering. Minimum: professional UX design experience, a portfolio of shipped work, and working knowledge of accessibility standards. Preferred: experience with insurance or financial services products.
slots.jd.insurance-digital.duties:
Responsibilities
- Identify accessibility issues across digital products and work with engineering to deliver fixes.
- Synthesize user research into clear findings and design recommendations.
- Plan and run usability sessions with policyholders, agents and internal users.
- Translate session results into revised designs and share them with stakeholders.
- Contribute to shared design standards and documentation.
slots.jd.insurance-digital.needs:
Minimum and preferred qualifications
- 5 or more years of experience in UX or product design.
- Proficiency in Figma and Adobe Illustrator.
- Wireframing and prototyping skills for web and mobile flows.
- A strong grounding in interaction design principles.
- Comfort giving and receiving feedback through design critique.
- Preferred: experience designing for insurance or financial services.
slots.r1.b1: Fixes accessibility issues directly in HTML and CSS across product screens, cutting open accessibility defects by 50 percent.
slots.r1.b2: Hands off designs to engineering with findings from usability testing attached, so open interaction questions are settled before build.
slots.r1.b3: Runs stakeholder reviews structured around design critique, reducing revision rounds by 20 percent.
slots.r1.b4: Produces wireframes in Adobe Illustrator to align product and engineering on layout before detailed design begins.
slots.r1.i1: At Oakmont Systems, runs usability sessions to test designs with users and turn the findings into product changes.
slots.r1.i2: UX Designer at Oakmont Systems responsible for handing finished designs off to engineering with clear specifications.
slots.r2.b1: Built design system components in Figma, cutting the time needed to assemble new screens by 50 percent.
slots.r2.b2: Synthesized user research findings into recommendations and fed them back into the team's design systems work.
slots.r2.b3: Ran usability sessions paired with accessibility review, raising task completion rates by 10 percent.
slots.r2.b4: Tracked accessibility fixes on shared Miro boards, keeping design and engineering aligned on each open issue.
slots.r2.i1: Supported handoff to engineering at Halcyon Services by preparing design files and notes for developers.
slots.r2.i2: Created wireframes at Halcyon Services that shaped early page layouts for product teams.
slots.summary.1: UX designer who owns a service end to end, from user research through wireframing to final layouts in Figma. Uses design critique and usability testing to keep work consistent and validated before handoff to engineering.
slots.summary.2: Mid-level product and UX designer experienced in owning a workstream from early wireframing to engineering handoff. Works in Figma and leads design critique sessions grounded in usability testing and accessibility review.
